Six fifty-nine a.m. Your alarm goes off.
You slap the snooze button. Same as every morning.
But this time... the beeping stops. And so does everything else.
Nev! You're gonna be late for—
Your mom is frozen on the stairs. Mid-word. Mid-step.
The orange juice she was pouring is hanging in the air. Like glass.
The clock says six fifty-nine. And it stays six fifty-nine.
What if your snooze button didn't give you nine more minutes of sleep... but nine minutes of frozen time? For everyone... except you.
Nine minutes later, everything snaps back.
School! Wait... why is the juice all over the floor?
Rule one: every snooze gives you exactly nine minutes. Nobody else moves.
Rule two: you can press it again. And again. The minutes stack.
Rule three: if you touch someone... they can move too.
You find that one out at the bus stop.
Bro. Bro! Why is the bus driver a statue? Why is that bird just... floating?
Jake's hand is still on your shoulder.
Okay. Okay. This is the best day of my life. Hahaha!
Five snoozes before a math test. Forty-five extra minutes to study. You get an A for the first time since fourth grade.
Nev... an A? Did you... study?
Ten snoozes at lunch. Jake eats everyone's fries. Every single tray.
It's not stealing if time is frozen. The law is frozen, bro. Hahaha!
You make him put them back. Mostly.
Twenty snoozes at night. Three hours of video games while the whole world waits.
By Friday, you've stacked a hundred and forty snoozes. Twenty-one extra hours.
Your week has eight days in it. And nobody notices.
Saturday, you try the big one. A hundred snoozes in a row. Fifteen hours of frozen time.
You walk downtown. A pigeon is frozen mid-flap. A guy is frozen mid-sneeze. You put your hat on him.
A hot dog guy is frozen mid-squeeze. The ketchup just hangs there in the air.
You eat the hot dog. You leave five dollars. You're not a monster.
You sleep in frozen time. Twelve hours of perfect sleep, and you're still early to school.
You read every book in the library. You learn guitar. You learn Spanish. Kind of.
Hola. Me llamo Nev. Son las... six fifty-nine.
Jake wants to use it for everything.
Dude, freeze the game! Right before the buzzer! We walk the ball into the hoop!
You do. The whole gym goes crazy.
Extra time: nine hundred hours. And counting.
Then, on day nineteen, your mom stops you at the door.
Honey... did you get taller? Like... since Monday?
You laugh. But at school, your jeans are too short.
Your hair is longer than Jake's. You got a haircut two weeks ago.
In the kitchen, there's a door where your mom marks your height every birthday.
Last mark: September. Today you're two inches above it.
Bro... is that a mustache? Since when do you have a mustache?
That night, you do the math.
Nine hundred hours of frozen time. That's thirty-seven days.
Thirty-seven days that only you lived through.
The calendar says three weeks have passed. Your body says two months.
Every snooze doesn't just freeze the world. It moves you forward.
You're getting older... while everyone you love is standing still.
And it's not just the haircut.
Jake tells you a joke at lunch. You heard it forty frozen hours ago. You forget to laugh.
Okay... you used to love that one.
Your mom's birthday is Saturday. For her, it's two days away. For you, it's two lonely weeks.
And then you notice something worse.
In frozen time, it's quiet. No birds. No cars. No voices.
Just you... and a clock that never moves.
You've spent more time alone this month than with anyone you know.
Mom? Mom... can you hear me?
She can't. She's frozen in the kitchen, smiling at something you said... thirty hours ago.
Monday morning. Six fifty-nine. The alarm rings.
Your hand moves to the snooze button by itself. Like a habit.
One more. Just nine minutes. What's nine minutes?
You've pressed it four thousand times.
You pull the plug. The clock goes dark.
And for the first time in two months... you're late.
It's the best detention of your life. Because the clock on the wall is moving.
Slowly. Normally. For everyone. Including you.
Wait. So you're two months older than me now? So I'm the baby? Hahaha... no way.
You laugh. At the right time.
But promise me one thing. If you ever freeze time again... you take me with you.
Saturday, you give your mom a birthday card. You wrote it on day twelve... of frozen time.
Oh, sweetie... it's beautiful. When did you find the time to write all this?
You smile. Some secrets are worth keeping.
Extra time: zero. And for the first time, that number feels good.
That night, you sleep with no alarm.
The clock you unplugged... is ringing.
On the screen, one word. Snoozed.
Outside, the rain is frozen in the air. The whole street is still.
Except for one window across the street... where somebody just turned on a light.
